newsitem.title: UK: Borrowers eye jumbo 10-year dollar bonds - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Borrowers eye jumbo 10-year dollar bonds - dealers.

text.p: A number of large Euromarket borrowers were eyeing the 10-year dollar sector as demand for longer-dated debt from institutional investors was boosted by the rise in U.S. interest rates, dealers said on Wednesday.
Canada, the Asian Development Bank (ADB), the World Bank, and Canadian provinces like Quebec were all possible candidates for bonds for up to $1.0 billion, they said.
Smaller issues could surface from Japanese borrowers.
"A lot of investors have been lengthening duration because with low inflation and rising rates you would expect the curve to remain flat or flatten further," a U.S. bank trader said.
He said expensive 10-year repos were making bond issues unattractive but this situation could ease.

"Borrowers will be keen to see whether or not the Fed will auction a new 10-year bond or add to existing paper, which will affect the repo market, and they need to keep an eye on economic data," he said.
"As long as U.S. inflation remains under control and growth is healthy we expect investors to buy into the sector," he said.

On Tuesday the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) raised the target for the fed funds rate by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent. The move, the first U.S. rate rise for over two years, was taken as a pre-emptive measure to head off inflation.

There has been relatively little supply in the 10-year dollar sector recently, apart from a $500 million deal from Kreditanstanlt fuer Wiederaufbau (KfW) and a $1.0 billion deal from the Inter-American Development Bank (IADB).
The IADB bond, launched in March, was priced at the historically tight level of 17 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
"The IADB is now trading in the low-20 b.p. over Treasuries," a syndicate manager at a European bank said.
"The recent correction and shake-out was very much necessary, and investors will be keener to buy at current spread levels," he said.
An ADB bond, still at least a few weeks away, was likely to be priced at around 20 b.p. over, dealers said.

Demand for dollar bonds from Asian institutions was also boosted by the strong dollar, dealers said, and the start of the new Japanese financial year in April would increase activity from that sector.
